questions.text:
Document cameras in classrooms use a concave lens as part of their projection system.

One such camera has an object 12 cm from a concave lens with focal length 8 cm.

Draw and label the image in the diagram below.
questions.expectedAnswer: Image found between F and the lens, on the same side as the object. Virtual, upright, diminished.

questions.text:
Calculate the magnification of the image.

(Object distance = 12 cm, focal length = -8 cm for concave lens)
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Uses correct formula. Merit: Correct magnification = 0.4.

questions.text: Fully describe the nature of the image formed.
questions.expectedAnswer: Image will be virtual, upright, and diminished.

questions.text:
In another camera lens assembly, a convex lens is used, and a real image three times as big as the object is formed.

Complete a ray diagram on the grid below to show how the real image that is three times as big as the object is formed.

You must show any calculations you used to decide where to place the object.

Make the object 4 squares tall.
questions.expectedAnswer: di/do = 3, so di = 3do. Using 1/f = 1/di + 1/do: do = 4f/3. hI = 12 squares.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: States di = 3do. Merit: Places object and image correctly. Excellence: Full diagram with calculations.

questions.text:
An ultra-short-throw camera lens assembly uses a concave mirror to reflect and focus light on a screen.

Complete the ray diagram to find and draw the image.
questions.expectedAnswer: Image located using two rays. Image is virtual, upright, and enlarged (object within F).
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Correct diagram. Merit: Diagram AND description.

questions.text: Describe the nature of the image formed by the concave mirror.
questions.expectedAnswer: Image is virtual, upright, and enlarged.

questions.text:
A laminated safety glass panel has two glass panes with a refractive index of 1.4, separated by an air gap. A student notices a red laser shone through doesn't travel straight.

Show the path of the ray as it crosses from one glass pane to the air.
questions.expectedAnswer: Ray bends away from the normal when passing from glass (denser) to air (less dense).

questions.text: Explain what a refractive index of 1.4 means, in terms of the speed of light in the glass.
questions.expectedAnswer: The speed of light is 1.4 times slower in glass than in air. v_glass = 3.0 x 10^8 / 1.4 = 2.14 x 10^8 m s-1.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Light is slower in glass. Merit: Quantitative answer.

questions.text:
Red laser with wavelength 6.30 x 10^-7 m enters a different window at an incident angle of 35 degrees. The wavelength in the glass is 4.50 x 10^-7 m.

Calculate the angle of refraction as the laser passes from air (n = 1.0) into the glass.
questions.expectedAnswer: n_glass = lambda_air/lambda_glass = 6.30e-7/4.50e-7 = 1.40. n1 sin theta1 = n2 sin theta2. 1.0 x sin 35 = 1.40 x sin theta2. sin theta2 = 0.5736/1.40 = 0.4097. theta2 = 24.2 degrees.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: n_glass = 1.40. Merit: One error. Excellence: Correct angle.

questions.text:
The student notices that increasing the angle causes total internal reflection.

Name the phenomenon.
Describe the conditions needed for this phenomenon.
questions.expectedAnswer: Light must travel from a medium of higher refractive index to lower refractive index. The angle of incidence must exceed the critical angle.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: One condition. Merit: Partial. Excellence: Full explanation.

questions.text:
Bluetooth connections work by sending information as electromagnetic waves.

What type of wave is an electromagnetic wave?

Bluetooth interference can occur when two devices are using the same frequency. This causes both spots of strong signal and weak signal.

Explain how two Bluetooth sources emitting the same frequency can cause this.
questions.expectedAnswer: When two waves of the same frequency overlap, they interfere. Constructive interference (waves in phase, path difference = whole wavelengths) produces strong signal. Destructive interference (waves out of phase, path difference = odd half wavelengths) produces weak signal.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Recognises interference. Merit: Partial explanation. Excellence: Full explanation with path difference.

questions.text:
Communication satellites orbit at 600 km altitude. The wavelength of the signal is 0.030 m.

How many radio waves reach the Earth in 3 hours?
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Correct frequency. Merit: Correct answer.

questions.text:
When signals pass through walls, they slow down. The boundary can be modelled by ropes of different densities.

Describe how the frequency of the signal changes as it moves from air to wall.
questions.expectedAnswer: The frequency does not change as the signal enters or leaves the wall.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Frequency unchanged. Merit: Frequency unchanged with justification.

questions.text: Assuming any pulse is half the height after transmission/reflection at the boundary, draw the result of two pulses' interactions after 3 seconds.
questions.expectedAnswer: Correct diagram showing transmitted and reflected pulses at correct positions after 3 seconds, with correct amplitudes (half of original).
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: One pulse positioned correctly. Merit: Two pulses correct. Excellence: Full diagram.
